newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro bourses mixed, rattled by rate jitters.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro bourses mixed, rattled by rate jitters.

text.p: European bourses put in a mixed performance on Thursday, unsettled by a negative close on Wall Street and still worried about the direction of interest rates.
On currency markets, the dollar clawed back losses against the yen after a sudden bout of nerves before next week's U.S. election caused profit-taking in early trading.
London stocks were down in the wake of Wednesday's surprise increase in British interest rates and French shares were slipping in and out profit for most of the morning.

London's FTSE index slipped 11.6 points to 3,952.3, its lowest for a month, before recovering slightly. Shares in companies with foreign trading were hit hardest amid concerns that earnings would suffer as sterling strengthened on the back of the rate hike.

"If you look at the domestic stocks, like the retailers, they're holding up," a dealer said. "People are just getting over the initial shock of the rate increase, but we're not seeing a lot of client interest."
The stock market was not overly-pessimistic. "We think the underlying trend is still strong. There is money out there, " said another trader.
Dealers said they did not expect London shares to move too much before a fresh run of U.S. data is released, giving clues on the health of the powerful American economy.
Investors will mainly be watching for potentially market-moving U.S. jobs figures for September on Friday. Data on U.S. income for September is due at 1330 GMT on Thursday.
The main European bourses, frequently influenced by movements on Wall Street, will also keep an anxious eye open for New York's performance after its 13.79-point loss to 5,993.23 points on Wednesday.
In Paris, French shares shrugged off a five-basis point cut in the intervention rate, against expectations of a 10-point cut, and kept the morning's modest gains.
The market had also not reacted to a rise in the franc after the European Commission said it would not object to France using a special France Telecom payment to cut its deficit.
Frankfurt stocks were the morning's poorest performers, dropping 0.8 percent in floor trading ahead of the U.S. figures.
The dollar strengthened against the yen in morning trade and traders were confident the dollar weakness was a blip in a trend that has carried it to 42-month highs against the Japanese currency.
"We've had a bit of a shakeout, a bit of a pullback, and now we're in a consolidation period before we start to look for the next move higher," said a trader at IBJ International in London.

"The main driving force behind this currency pair is Japanese investors and their need to invest abroad to enhance yield, and we see this continuing," said Stuart Thomson, chief international economist at Nikko Europe in London.
Analysts said the market was fearful U.S. Democrats would seize control of Congress on November 5, ushering in an era of looser fiscal and trade policy.
The pound sterling came off its highs hit after the interest rate increase. It was at $1.6279 by mid-day, down half a cent on Wednesday's 19-month peak against the dollar.
In Johannesburg, the South African rand slumped to new all-time lows in early trade before bouncing back seven cents as speculators rushed to take profits.
Dealers said investors who had sold the rand short earlier in the week scrambled to pocket their gains after it hit a lowest ever 4.7695 against the dollar.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was trading around 1.5128 marks and 113.86 yen versus 1.5095 and 113.89 in late European business on Wednesday.
STOCKS AT 1230 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was down 5.2 points at 3,958.7.
Germany's DAX index was 20.07 lower at 2,658.66.
In Paris, the CAC 40 index was up 2.69 at 2127.45.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed weaker at $379.30 an ounce, compared with $380.05 at Wednesday's close. Silver was at $4.81, down two cents.
